nodes.name: Arc melting of multiphase alloy
nodes.procedure: First, the high-purity metal cylindrical particles, including Al, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Nb, Mo, Ta, W, are mixed according to a specified formula. The particles, with diameters ranging from 2 to 4 mm and heights of 2 to 5 mm, are then weighed and placed into a copper crucible inside a high-vacuum arc furnace. The furnace chamber is first prepumped using a mechanical pump, and then a molecular pump is used to achieve a high vacuum level of 4×10^{-4} Pa. After reaching the vacuum, argon gas is introduced to the furnace to maintain a pressure of 0.03 to 0.05 MPa. The electric arc is initiated using the buried arc technique, and the titanium ingot is remelted two to four times to eliminate oxygen from the chamber. Last, after the titanium ingot is remelted, the alloy raw materials are melted. During the arc melting process, magnetic stirring was used to ensure thorough mixing and homogenization of the materials. After melting, the alloys were cooled to room temperature in a copper crucible within the arc melting furnace.

nodes.procedure: The alloys corresponding to alloys I to VII were synthesized using the arc melting technique without undergoing additional physical or chemical treatments. The particles, with diameters ranging from 2 to 4 mm and heights of 2 to 5 mm, are then weighed and placed into a copper crucible inside a high-vacuum arc furnace. After reaching the vacuum, argon gas is introduced to the furnace to maintain a pressure of 0.03 to 0.05 MPa. The electric arc is initiated using the buried arc technique, and the titanium ingot is remelted two to four times to eliminate oxygen from the chamber. Last, after the titanium ingot is remelted, the alloy raw materials are melted. During the arc melting process, magnetic stirring was used to ensure thorough mixing and homogenization of the materials. After melting, the alloys were cooled to room temperature in a copper crucible within the arc melting furnace.

nodes.name: Post-processing of alloys
nodes.procedure: The synthesized membrane electrode assemblies were subjected to electrical discharge machining and cut into dimensions of 1 mm by 5 mm by 8 mm. The samples were then processed through grinding using SiC sandpapers. Initially, 100# sandpaper was used for coarse grinding to remove surface oxidation layers. This was followed by a sequence of finer sandpapers (200#, 400#, 800#, 1200#, and 2000#) to eliminate residual surface stress layers. Water was used as a medium during each grinding step to prevent excessive heat generation and potential damage to the samples. Upon completion of grinding, the samples were polished to a smooth finish using sandpaper. Last, the samples were ultrasonically cleaned in anhydrous ethanol to remove any remaining grinding particles and contaminants.

nodes.description: CV activation for surface reconstruction assessment
nodes.source_text: we activated the multiphase alloy using cyclic voltammetry (CV) from −1.5 to 1 V (Hg/HgO), followed by SEM surface observation (Fig. 3A and fig. S17). The results show distinct modifications of different phases on the alloy surface, with phase 1 exhibiting substantial surface reconstruction.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH after CV activation
nodes.source_text: The catalytic OER properties of alloys with compositions of alloys I to VI and the multiphase alloy were characterized by a three-electrode configuration at room temperature in a 1 M KOH electrolyte. As illustrated in Fig. 4 (A to C), after CV activation, alloy I exhibited the lowest overpotential and Tafel slope... overpotential of alloy I is as low as only 199 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2... Tafel slope of 52.8 mV dec−1... at a high current density of 100 mA cm−2, alloy I maintained an almost constant potential for at least 1200 hours

potential_evolution.value: decreases markedly initial cycles, stabilizes ~1.45 V vs RHE

nodes.source_text: We also investigated the process of CV activation; as the number of CV cycles increases, the overpotentials of different alloys show substantial differences (Fig. 4D). The potential of alloy I decreases markedly in the initial few tens cycles and stabilizes in the subsequent 300 cycles, eventually settling at ∼1.45 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE).
